parameters.label: Report
parameters.description: jfb_reports row id for this day

parameters.name: projectFilter
parameters.label: Project filter
parameters.description: Caller-built: {"id": "<projectId>"}

parameters.name: reportFilter
parameters.label: Report filter
parameters.description: Caller-built: {"report_id": "<reportId>"}

parameters.name: equipmentFilter
parameters.label: Equipment filter
parameters.description: Caller-built: {"project_id": "<projectId>", "id": [<equipment ids on this report date>]} -- only active equipment whose mobilized_on/demobilized_on window includes the report date, matching the non-native app's fetchProjectEquipment(projectId, reportDate). A placeholder all-zero id is sent when no equipment applies, because an empty id list is rejected by the read.

parameters.name: narrativeSections
parameters.label: Narrative sections
parameters.description: Caller-resolved ordered [{label, content}], one per configured jfb_project_report_narratives section for this project. Resolved client-side (not a domain-query source) because jfb_report_narratives_v2 has no sort_order of its own -- order lives on the separate template domain, joined by label.

parameters.name: dailyActivityByEquipment
parameters.label: Daily activity by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-resolved {equipmentId: {lead, columns, rows}} -- the whole Daily Activity table, shaped so the template never branches on discipline. `columns` is the tail column list after Minutes and differs by the equipment's resolved work type: a DREDGE sheet prints Area, Pass, Event, Notes (reference's ProductionSheetPage.tsx ACTIVITY_COL) and a CAPPING sheet prints Pass, <area label>, Lane, Step, Event, Notes (reference's CappingProductionSheetPage.tsx CAP_ACTIVITY_COL) -- Lane and Step describe a hydraulic capping spreader working a numbered lane in numbered steps and exist only on the capping sheet. The capping sheet's area column is headed by the project's own noun for a level-1 area -- jfb_project_area_levels.label at depth 1 (Torch Lake calls them DMUs, Penobscot subareas), falling back to "Area". The dredge sheet's header is the constant "Area", as in the reference. The reference app carries this noun on a projects.area_label column instead; this app has no such column because the area-levels domain already models it per depth, and is edited at Admin -> Projects -> Area Level Labels. `lead` carries the widths of the fixed #/From/To/Minutes columns, which differ between the two variants. Each row is {num, from, to, minutes, cells:[{v, cls}], pad?}; `cells` is in `columns` order and `cls` is the per-column alignment class, so a row needs no knowledge of which variant it belongs to. A CAPPING sheet lists only the non-productive rows -- delays, startup/shutdown, moves -- because productive placement time is already summarized in its Production Totals block, and pads to 12 when <=10 real rows (reference's selectCapActivityDensity); a DREDGE sheet pads to 15 when <=12 (selectActivityDensity). Padded rows carry pad:true so the row number prints gray, as in the reference. Discipline is resolved per equipment via equipmentWorkType(). Resolved client-side because it needs timezone-aware calendar-day matching (jfb_daily_activities has no report_id/date column), a two-hop delay-code lookup, and a pass label that may come from either pkl-jfb-pass-type or pkl-jfb-lift -- none of them reachable from a domain-query filter or this engine's Handlebars.

parameters.name: delaySummaryByEquipment
parameters.label: Delay summary by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-resolved {equipmentId: [{description, minutes, percent}]}, computed from the same activities as dailyActivityByEquipment: non-productive rows grouped by category/delay-code label (first/last STARTUP-SHUTDOWN row broken out as Startup/ShutDown), sorted by minutes descending. Matches the non-native app's buildDelaySummary.

parameters.name: photoAssets
parameters.label: Photo assets
parameters.description: Caller-resolved {"1": {label, dataUri}|null, "2": {...}|null}, one per uploaded jfb_report_photos slot for this report. Resolved client-side via downloadAttachment() + base64 data-URI conversion, because the render engine's domain-query sources return only the photo_file_path file id, not file bytes, and the Asset Manifest only supports a fixed fileId set at publish time, not one that changes per report.

parameters.name: dredgeChartAssets
parameters.label: Dredge chart page by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-resolved {equipmentId: {dataUri, equipmentName, projectName, dateISO}}, present for every DREDGING equipment on this project as of this report date and ABSENT for capping/placement equipment. The template's whole Daily Dredge Progress Chart page hangs off this lookup, so an omitted key drops the page entirely -- a placement machine has no dredge chart by definition and used to print "No dredge progress chart generated" on a page of its own. dataUri is null when the PE never saved a jfb_dredge_progress.chart_path for the day, which is what prints that placeholder for a dredge. Discipline is resolved per equipment via equipmentWorkType() (pinned jfb_equipments.work_type, else the project's dated phase), never from project.work_type. Each entry carries its own page header/footer strings so the template never walks back out of the {{#with}} block. Built by buildDredgeChartAssetsParam() in reportPdfData.js; images are downloaded and base64 data-URI converted client-side, same pattern as photoAssets.

parameters.name: safetyPageData
parameters.label: Safety page data
parameters.description: Caller-resolved object binding the whole Safety Report sheet: the 7(+1) Daily Safety Updates fields (Culture Tenant resolved to "name: description", next-day summary included only when project.show_next_day_summary), jfb_report_crew_summary_v2 rows, jfb_project_site_equipment rows mobilized as of this report's date, and both signatures as data URIs. Resolved client-side (not a domain-query source) because Culture Tenant needs a join and equipment needs an as-of-date window filter, neither expressible as a single domain-query source or in this engine's Handlebars. Also includes crewTotals (totalCount/todayHours from this report's own crew rows, previousProjectHours/totalProjectHours derived from dvw-jfb-crew-hours-total-v2, a project-lifetime no-date-filter sum -- mirrors the reference app's PDF-only cumulative crew-hours figures) and a climate object (temp/wind/precip, Precip MTD/Project Total via dvw-jfb-precip-sums-v2, conditions), each field pre-formatted with a unit string or an em dash fallback matching the reference app's PDF convention.

parameters.name: opSummaryByEquipment
parameters.label: Operator/shift summary by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-computed {equipmentId: {operator, shiftFrom, shiftTo}} -- dominant operator (most logged minutes that day) and shift bounds (earliest start / latest end), derived from the same activity rows dailyActivityByEquipment already carries.

parameters.name: productionStatsByEquipment
parameters.label: Production stats by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-computed {equipmentId: {columns: [comboLabel...], rows: [{label, total, values: [...]}], headline: {goh, noh, delay}}}, one row per metric, present for every project equipment. 'values' is in the same order as 'columns'; 'headline' is a convenience copy of the day's whole-equipment GOH/NOH/Delay for the sheet's 3 big stat boxes, which need one named value each rather than a row walk. The row SET depends on the equipment's own resolved work type (equipmentWorkType(): pinned jfb_equipments.work_type, else the project's dated phase from placement_start_date/prior_work_type -- never project.work_type), so a mixed-phase project prints a dredge sheet for its dredge and a capping sheet for its placement unit on the same daily. The template renders either with no branching. DREDGE rows (GOH/NOH/Delay/Efficiency/Area/Volume/CY-per-GOH/CY-per-NOH/SF-per-GOH/SF-per-NOH/Area-descriptor) match the reference app's ProductionSheetPage.tsx: activities are the sole source of combo identity (production_stats rows are only matched onto an already-built combo by area+pass+tsca, never used to originate one -- an unmatched stats row is dropped from the per-combo breakdown, same as reference, though it still counts toward 'Total' which sums every stats row independent of the breakdown), and each combo column is that day's breakdown by work combo (area+pass+tsca+attachment) actually logged. CAPPING rows (GOH/NOH/Efficiency/Tons-per-GOH/Tons-per-NOH/Area SF/Acres/Design Tons/Tons Placed/CY Placed/Estimated Inches/Material Placed/Pass/Area) match the reference app's CappingProductionSheetPage.tsx CAP_ROWS: one column per SUBAREA worked (subarea x layer on a multi-layer project, hours measured per layer from the events when they carry one and pro-rata by tonnage when they don't), GOH/NOH summed from that subarea's activities so the sheet reconciles to the event log by construction, Acres = SF/43,560, Estimated Inches = CY*324/SF, and Design Tons = SF placed * (jfb_project_areas.volume_goal_cy / area_goal_sf for the level-1 area) * factor. The three CY-derived rows (CY Placed / Estimated Inches / Design Tons) are DROPPED entirely when the project has no cap_conversion_factor and no column carries CY -- on a tonnage-paid contract they are zero by construction, and printing '0.0' down every column reads as broken data rather than 'not applicable'. Roll-ups count only production rows carrying a real entry, because this app pre-seeds a capping row per equipment x leaf area x layer. Built by buildProductionComboTotalsByEquipmentParam() in reportPdfData.js from jfb_daily_activities + this report's jfb_production_stats rows, grouped via src/lib/productionCombos.js (same grouping logic the on-screen Production Stats tab uses).

parameters.name: productionTotals
parameters.label: Cover production metrics
parameters.description: Caller-computed {rows: [{label, unit, day, week, project}]}, one row per fixed metric (Total Volume Removed/CY, Total Area Covered/SF, Operating Hours/hrs, Delay Hours/hrs, Efficiency/%). Matches the reference app's cover-page Project Production Table exactly: Day is today's value (null/em-dash if no released report or no activity logged that day), Week sums Sunday-of-this-week through today, Project sums the whole project history through today. Efficiency is a ratio of summed GOH/NOH over each window, not an average of daily efficiencies. Built by buildCoverProductionTotalsParam() in reportPdfData.js from dvw-jfb-realized-daily-totals-v2 (released reports only, same view Weekly Summary/Realized To-Date use).

parameters.name: weekday
parameters.label: Weekday name
parameters.description: Long weekday name (e.g. "Friday") for the report date, shown above the date in the cover/sheet date tables.

parameters.name: projectWeek
parameters.label: Project week number
parameters.description: 1-indexed week relative to project.start_date; null when start_date is unset.

parameters.name: productionWeek
parameters.label: Production week number
parameters.description: 1-indexed Sunday-anchored week relative to project.production_start_date, for the production sheet's "Prod. Wk #" column. Sunday-Saturday weeks counted from the Sunday on or before production_start_date, matching the reference app's productionWeekNumber(). Falls back to projectWeek when the project has no production_start_date, the same fallback chain the reference uses. Only the Production Report sheets read this; the cover's "Project Wk. #" and the Safety/Water/Air headers stay on projectWeek, which is what the reference app prints there.

parameters.name: reportNumberByEquipment
parameters.label: Report number by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-computed {equipmentId: '<YYMMDD><initials>'}, matching the reference app's reportNumber = compactDate(report_date) + nameInitials(equipment.name). Built by buildEquipmentReportNumbers() in reportPdfData.js.

parameters.name: projectStartDate
parameters.label: Project start date (pretty)
parameters.description: Pretty-formatted (e.g. "Aug 1, 2026") copy of project.start_date, from buildDateTableParams(). Falls back to the raw project.start_date timestamp if project data has not loaded.

parameters.name: flowStatsByEquipment
parameters.label: Flow stats by equipment
parameters.description: Caller-computed {equipmentId: {avgVelocityFps, avgFlowRateGpm, dailyTotalGal, previousTotalGal, projectTotalGal}|absent}. Matches the reference app's buildFlowStats() exactly: Previous/Project Total Flow sum jfb_hydraulic_flow_stats.daily_total_gal (a directly PE-entered value, not derived) across this equipment's history through yesterday/today; an equipment with neither a reading today nor any prior history is omitted entirely (template falls back to 'Pending data entry'). Built by buildFlowAndPipeByEquipmentParam() in reportPdfData.js.

parameters.name: pipeSegments
parameters.label: Pipe segments (today)
parameters.description: Caller-computed [{id, name, lengthFt}], project-wide (jfb_hydraulic_pipe_configurations has no equipment_id) -- same list rendered on every equipment's sheet for this report date, matching reference's own project-wide pipeRows. Built by buildFlowAndPipeByEquipmentParam().

parameters.name: pipeTotalLength
parameters.label: Pipe total length (today)
parameters.description: Caller-computed sum of pipeSegments[].lengthFt, formatted. Built by buildFlowAndPipeByEquipmentParam().

parameters.name: coverDensity
parameters.label: Cover density tier
parameters.description: Cover-page density tier -- one of normal/compact/dense/ultra -- chosen by pickDensity() in src/pages/FieldOps/lib/coverDensity.js, a direct port of the non-native app's estimateHeight.ts. It estimates the cover stack's height from narrative character counts (newlines counted separately) plus the production-table row count, and returns the LOOSEST tier that still fits the 720pt content budget. Emitted as a `cover-<tier>` class on .cover-frame, which the cover-density CSS blocks scale against. Upstream flags the estimator as a heuristic rather than an authoritative measurement, so a cover can still run long in the rare case where even the tightest tier overflows.

parameters.name: waterQuality
parameters.label: Water Monitoring page
parameters.description: Caller-resolved Daily Water Monitoring page, or null when the project has no jfb_water_monitoring_config row or the date pulled no readings -- the same gate the reference app uses, so a project without monitoring prints exactly as before. Holds the fixed-role (compliance) reading table {timeLabel, background, earlyWarning, compliance, delta} pre-formatted to 2dp, the average background-minus-compliance difference, the configured monitor coordinates, the PE's notes and daily reference NTU from jfb_water_monitoring_notes, the derived Response Action / Not-to-Exceed limits, and the turbidity chart plus station aerial as data URIs. Built by buildWaterQualityParam() in reportPdfData.js, reusing lib/waterQuality so the PDF and the on-screen tab cannot disagree. The reference app's TIDAL variant is not included: no project has tide data and the native app has no tidal data layer.

parameters.name: airQuality
parameters.label: Air Monitoring page
parameters.description: Caller-resolved Daily Air Monitoring page, or null when the project has no jfb_air_monitoring_config row or the date pulled no readings. Holds the config's Equipment / Calibration Information / Notes text blocks, the PE's project-activity line and notes from jfb_air_monitoring_daily, and three images as data URIs: the annotated station aerial plus the LLRA and Mineral Building Property PM10 charts, both rendered portrait (900x1150) to sit side by side on the bottom half of the page, matching the Excel-era export. Built by buildAirQualityParam() in reportPdfData.js, reusing lib/airQuality so the PDF and the on-screen tab cannot disagree.
